q-3749.name: Question 1
q-3749.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{-2{x}^{4}+6{x}^{2}-4}{{x}^{2}-1} & =\frac{-2(1)^{4}+6(1)^{2}-4}{(1)^{2}-1}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-2{x}^{4}+6{x}^{2}-4}{{x}^{2}-1} & =\frac{-2({x}^{4}-3{x}^{2}+2)}{{x}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{-2({x}^{2}-2)({x}^{2}-1)}{{x}^{2}-1} \\  & =-2({x}^{2}-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{-2{x}^{4}+6{x}^{2}-4}{{x}^{2}-1} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\,\,-2({x}^{2}-2) \\  & =-2(1-2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

limx→1−2x4+6x2−4x2−1=−2(1)4+6(1)2−4(1)2−1=00

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. −2x4+6x2−4x2−1=−2(x4−3x2+2)x2−1=−2(x2−2)(x2−1)x2−1=−2(x2−2).

Therefore, limx→1−2x4+6x2−4x2−1=limx→1−2(x2−2)=−2(1−2)=2.

q-101160.name: Question 2
q-101160.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to 3}\frac{{y}^{2}+3y-18}{{y}^{2}-3y} & =\frac{{3}^{2}+3(3)-18}{{3}^{2}-3(3)}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}+3y-18}{{y}^{2}-3y} & =\frac{(y+6)(y-3)}{y(y-3)} \\  & =\frac{y+6}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to 3}\frac{{y}^{2}+3y-18}{{y}^{2}-3y} & ={lim}_{y\to 3}\frac{y+6}{y} \\  & =\frac{3+6}{3} \\  & =\frac{9}{3} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

q-313149.name: Question 3
q-313149.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -2}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x-14}{x+2} & =\frac{(-2)^{2}-5(-2)-14}{-2+2} \\  & =\frac{4+10-14}{0} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-5x-14}{x+2} & =\frac{(x-7)(x+2)}{x+2} \\  & =x-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -2}(x-7) & =(-2)-7 \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$
